mainEntity.name: Do I need a paid AI generator for this exercise?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. You can write the script and storyboard in a text editor and use simple shapes for the visuals. If you choose a generation tool, check its current usage charges and export limits first.

mainEntity.name: Why did my automated avatar video fail when the manual one worked?

acceptedAnswer.text: Automation adds limits the studio does not show. In my HeyGen build the API rejected videos over 180 seconds on my plan, and a retrained avatar had a new ID. Check the API plan limits and the IDs the automation uses before relying on it.

mainEntity.name: What should I check before publishing an AI-assisted video?

acceptedAnswer.text: Compare every factual claim with the source, review the complete export, correct captions and crops, and confirm permission for the faces, voices, music and images you used.

mainEntity.name: Does a higher click-through rate always mean a better video?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Read click-through rate beside impressions, traffic sources and viewing behavior. Different audiences and observation windows can produce different rates, and a click does not show whether the video delivered its promise.

mainEntity.name: Can I diagnose a competitor’s retention from public views?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Public view counts do not reveal a channel’s private retention report. Use your own YouTube Studio analytics for a retention review and treat outside estimates as research clues.

pages.excerpt: Home Guides Build apps with AI coding agents: a safe first workflow Build guide · By Mike Holp · Published November 5, 2026 · Updated November 7, 2026 Build apps with AI coding agents: a safe first workflow Quick answer: give a coding agent one testable feature at a time. mainEntity.name: Does the example call a real AI provider?

mainEntity.name: What results should I expect?

acceptedAnswer.text: A wrong key returns HTTP 401, an unknown model returns HTTP 404 and a valid request returns HTTP 200, followed by a PASS line.

mainEntity.name: Is a chat subscription the same as an API key?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. A chat subscription covers the provider’s chat product, a provider API key has its own billing and limits, and a gateway key only gives access to your router. Anthropic, for example, bills API usage separately from paid Claude plans.

mainEntity.name: Where should I keep a real API key?

acceptedAnswer.text: In a server-side environment variable. Never place it in browser JavaScript, a public repository or a screenshot.

mainEntity.name: Why was ChatGPT Pro 20x paused?

acceptedAnswer.text: In September 2026, demand for GPT-6 Astra outran OpenAI’s capacity, so it paused new sign-ups to the $200 plan.

mainEntity.name: I already pay for Pro 20x. Do I lose it?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Existing subscribers kept access when sales were paused in September 2026. As of October 31, 2026, OpenAI’s help center says the allowance reduction it announced on September 29 is canceled: subscribers who had the higher allowance keep it, and the lower allowance has doubled to match. The $200 price stays the same.

mainEntity.name: Which Pro plan could you still buy?

acceptedAnswer.text: During the September 2026 pause, the 5x plan at about $100 per month. People on Plus or Pro 5x could no longer upgrade to 20x.

mainEntity.name: How many messages does each plan get?

acceptedAnswer.text: In September 2026, per the video, each 5-hour window gave Plus about 5 to 45 messages, Pro $100 about 25 to 225, and Pro 20x about 100 to 900. OpenAI’s pricing docs now say “Pro plans currently have no five-hour limit,” though weekly limits may apply.

mainEntity.name: Is ChatGPT Pro 20x available again?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. As of October 31, 2026, OpenAI’s help center says Pro 200 is available for new subscriptions again at $200 a month, and new subscriptions include the increased Work and Codex allowance. When I recorded the video on September 11, nobody knew how long the pause would last.

mainEntity.name: How do Codex credits work?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your plan’s included usage is used first, then your credit balance. Credits cover eligible Codex usage beyond your plan, and how fast they go depends on the model and task. Plus has limited GPT-6 Astra usage in Codex and can buy credits for more. Check your balance under Settings → Usage, or with /status in the CLI.

mainEntity.name: How do I make my credits last longer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use medium reasoning effort for most work. Save high for hard debugging, and avoid extra high and max for routine tasks.

mainEntity.name: What is 9Router?

acceptedAnswer.text: 9Router is a gateway between coding tools and model providers. Its official site describes a dashboard for managing providers, keys, combos and usage.

mainEntity.name: What should I test first?

acceptedAnswer.text: Test one provider and one model with a short prompt. Record the time, inspect the response, and find the corresponding request before adding fallbacks.

mainEntity.name: What is a model combo?

acceptedAnswer.text: The README describes a named sequence of models that can switch when quota is exhausted or an error occurs. Use the combo name as the requested model.

mainEntity.name: How many connections can I run?

acceptedAnswer.text: A universal simultaneous-connection limit was not verified in the reviewed documentation. Start with one active request and investigate the exact error before increasing parallel work.

mainEntity.name: Does the cost dashboard prove savings?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Compare a fixed task, its result, and the provider’s billing record before claiming savings. Keep measured charges separate from estimates.

mainEntity.name: Where are the official 9Router docs?

acceptedAnswer.text: The CLI README points to the GitHub repository as the full documentation, and the project website is 9router.com. The main README covers the API, client integrations, combos, environment variables and troubleshooting.

mainEntity.name: How do I update 9Router?

acceptedAnswer.text: The CLI runs an auto-update check when it starts, and 9router --skip-update skips that check. If you run the Docker image, the README lists docker pull decolua/9router:latest to update to the latest image. Write down the version before and after updating.

mainEntity.name: Which port does 9Router use, and can I change it?

acceptedAnswer.text: With default settings the dashboard opens at http://localhost:20128 and the API at http://localhost:20128/v1. The CLI accepts 9router --port 8080 for a custom port. If the dashboard opens on the wrong port, the README suggests setting PORT=20128 and NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:20128. If you change the port, update the base URL in every connected client as well.

mainEntity.name: How much does OpenCode Go cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Go costs $10 a month, Go Plus $40 a month and Go Teams $20 per member per month, as listed on November 1, 2026. Token prices are the same on every plan; the plans differ in how much usage each model includes.

mainEntity.name: What models are in OpenCode Go?

acceptedAnswer.text: About 30 models, mainly open coding models such as GLM, Kimi, DeepSeek, Qwen, MiniMax and MiMo, plus Grok 4.7, GPT 6 Luna, GPT 5.6 Luna, Claude Haiku 5.5 and Gemini 4 Argon. The list changes, so check the models endpoint or the Go page.

mainEntity.name: What are the OpenCode Go usage limits?

acceptedAnswer.text: Each model has a monthly allowance in dollars. You can use up to 20% of it in any 5 hours, 50% in a week and 100% in a month. Allowances range from $15 to $100 a month per model on Go, and are higher on Go Plus.

mainEntity.name: Is OpenCode Go the same as OpenCode Zen?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Zen is pay as you go from a credit balance and includes frontier models. Go is a monthly subscription with per-model limits on a curated set of open and low-cost models.

mainEntity.name: Do I need OpenCode Go to use OpenCode?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. OpenCode is free and open source, and works with other providers, local models and its own free models. Go is an optional provider.

mainEntity.name: Can I use OpenCode Go in Claude Code or Hermes?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. OpenCode lists Claude Code, Codex, Hermes v0.21.6 or later, Pi, jcode, ZCode and the Kilo Code CLI as validated clients, without guaranteeing they will keep working. Clients should send normal coding-agent traffic with their own user agent and a session ID.

mainEntity.name: What happens when I reach the limit?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can keep using the free models, or turn on Extra Usage on the Go page so requests fall back to your pay-as-you-go balance. Extra Usage needs credits in your console balance.

itemListElement.name: OpenRouter: API key, free models, pricing and setup

mainEntity.name: How do I get an OpenRouter API key?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sign up at openrouter.ai, open Settings › Keys and create a key. Add credits on the Credits page if you want paid models; free models work without a purchase, within their daily caps.

mainEntity.name: Is OpenRouter free?

acceptedAnswer.text: Signing up is free, and models ending in :free cost nothing. They are limited to 20 requests a minute and 50 a day, or 1,000 a day after you have bought at least 10 credits. Paid models draw from your credit balance.

mainEntity.name: How much does OpenRouter charge?

acceptedAnswer.text: Model usage is billed at the provider’s listed price with no markup. Buying credits carries a 5.5% fee with a $0.80 minimum, or 5% for crypto. Using your own provider keys is free up to $25,000 a month of usage, then 5%.

mainEntity.name: Why do I get a 402 error on a free model?

acceptedAnswer.text: A negative credit balance can block requests to free models too. Add credits to bring the balance above zero. The error’s limit_source field tells you whether the balance, a key limit or in-flight requests caused it.

mainEntity.name: Can I use OpenRouter with Claude Code?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Set ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL to https://openrouter.ai/api, put your OpenRouter key in ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN and set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY to an empty string. OpenRouter only guarantees this with Anthropic as the provider.

mainEntity.name: Do more API keys raise my rate limit?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. OpenRouter applies limits to your account as a whole. Separate keys help you track and cap spending per tool, not get more requests.

mainEntity.name: Which Claude model should I use?

acceptedAnswer.text: Start with Claude Opus 5.5 for most coding and agent work, which is what Anthropic recommends. Use Sonnet 5.5 when you want faster, cheaper turns, Haiku 5.5 for high-volume simple tasks, and Fable 5.1 only for the hardest long-running work.

mainEntity.name: Is Claude Opus better than Sonnet?

acceptedAnswer.text: Opus 5.5 is stronger on long, complex agentic work and costs twice as much per token. Sonnet 5.5 is close on many coding benchmarks and is faster, so it is the better value for well-scoped fixes and frequent coding turns.

mainEntity.name: How much do Claude models cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of November 3, 2026, per million input and output tokens: Fable 5.1 $10 and $50, Opus 5.5 $4 and $20, Sonnet 5.5 $2 and $10, and Haiku 5.5 from $0.10 and $0.50. Batch requests are 50% off.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between Claude Fable and Opus?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fable 5.1 is the most capable model for demanding reasoning and long-horizon agent work, at $10 and $50 per million tokens. Opus 5.5 costs $4 and $20 and performs at a similar level on most work, so try it first.

mainEntity.name: How do I change the model in Claude Code?

acceptedAnswer.text: Type /model in a Claude Code session and pick the model, then type /effort to set the effort level. Models your plan does not include ask you to add usage credits.

mainEntity.name: What is Claude Haiku good for?

acceptedAnswer.text: Haiku 5.5 suits narrow, high-volume tasks: classification, extraction, routing, customer support and acting as a sub-agent for Opus or Sonnet. It is the fastest and cheapest current Claude model.

itemListElement.name: What Is AI Automation? Examples, Tools and a First Build

mainEntity.name: What is AI automation?

acceptedAnswer.text: AI automation combines rules-based steps with an AI task such as classification, extraction or drafting, then checks the result before taking an action.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between AI automation and regular automation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Regular automation follows explicit rules. AI automation adds interpretation of inputs such as written messages, while rules still control validation and routing.

mainEntity.name: What are examples of AI automation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Examples include email triage, form classification, report drafts, YouTube description drafts and invoice data extraction. Each needs a trigger, an AI step and a checked output.

mainEntity.name: What are the best AI automation tools for beginners?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no single best tool. Zapier and Make both list a Free plan and use visual field mapping; n8n offers a free Community edition if you can self-host. Zapier says publishing an AI by Zapier step needs an eligible paid plan, so check each platform’s current plan page before building.

mainEntity.name: Can I use AI automation for free?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can practice with fictional inputs and check the free options described above. Confirm the platform allowance and model charges separately before running a connected workflow.

mainEntity.name: Is AI automation the same as AI agents?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. A fixed AI workflow follows a sequence you define. An agent has more freedom to choose its next step, and can be part of a larger workflow.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to code to build AI automations?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not for every workflow. You can begin with visual field mapping and routing, but you still need to define inputs, check outputs and handle failures.

schemas.headline: How does agentic AI differ from traditional automation?
schemas.description: Agentic AI picks its own steps toward a goal. Traditional automation follows a fixed path. See the differences, when to use each, and how to combine them.

itemListElement.name: How does agentic AI differ from traditional automation?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between agentic AI and traditional automation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Traditional automation follows a fixed path. Agentic AI chooses its next step toward a goal, within the tools and instructions it is given.

mainEntity.name: When should I use traditional automation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use a fixed workflow when the steps are predictable, the inputs are structured, and the result can be checked with clear rules.

mainEntity.name: When might an AI agent help?

acceptedAnswer.text: An agent may help when inputs vary and a task needs interpretation or a choice among bounded actions. A person should be able to review important outcomes.

mainEntity.name: Can an automation combine fixed steps and an AI agent?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A hybrid can put an agent step inside a fixed workflow, with validation and routing around it.

mainEntity.name: How can I test an agentic workflow safely?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use a small set of sample messages, validate outputs before actions, and check what happens when input is incomplete or the result is wrong.

mainEntity.name: What is Treg?

acceptedAnswer.text: The recording uses the Plugins panel to find and add Treg. Use the current supported connector setup and private sign-in fields, since interface labels can change.

mainEntity.name: Is Treg free?

acceptedAnswer.text: Treg is open source. Calls on Treg's keys are paid from a prepaid balance. Check the current account and endpoint terms. An introductory offer does not establish that every account or keyword route is eligible.

mainEntity.name: Can I use my own SEMrush or DataForSEO account?

acceptedAnswer.text: The recording demonstrates connecting DataForSEO credentials. Check the current provider connection and billing policy before relying on the same route for another account.

mainEntity.name: Does my bot see my API keys?

acceptedAnswer.text: Treg says provider credentials are injected server-side. Protect the separate Treg connection token as well, and inspect the specific integration’s access scope.

The presenter finds the n8n version more detailed with cleaner text, but NotebookLM is quicker for a one-off. The n8n template is in the presenter's paid community tiers.

14:37 Jan 23, 2026 245 views Make Viral YouTube Thumbnails In Minutes With NanoBanana! Make YouTube thumbnails with Nano Banana Pro through KIE: ChatGPT writes a thumbnail prompt, KIE regenerates an existing thumbnail from it at 16:9 and 1K, and Gemini swaps in the presenter's face with a wide-open-mouth expression. Each run costs about 18 credits, roughly 30 images for $5. The thumbnails are replaced on three videos with starting click-through rates around 3.3 to 3.8 percent, but no new rates are shown, and one face swap fails.

17:17 Jan 12, 2026 889 views Automate Your Entire Music Video Production with Suno & N8N An n8n workflow that takes a music genre from a form, writes a Suno prompt with OpenAI, generates instrumental tracks and a Nano Banana Pro background image through the KIE API, then assembles a video in Creatomate and saves it to Google Drive. Everything works up to the Creatomate step, which errors in the demo and still needs debugging.

13:07 Jan 12, 2026 258 views Making AI Videos Without Showing Your Face (Syllaby Tutorial) A live first test of Syllaby on a free trial: set the style, voice, music and subtitles, use a custom topic to script a one-minute faceless video about low-cost places for digital nomads, wait about three minutes for it to render and publish it to YouTube from inside Syllaby. An application error appears but the video still renders. Results are unknown, and the cost-of-living claims in the AI script are not checked. The link is an affiliate link.

41:21 Dec 27, 2025 1,463 views HeyGen AI Avatar Tutorial: Build Your First Video Without Filming! A course-style HeyGen tutorial: train an avatar from a short consented recording, add a voice clone from ElevenLabs through an API key, make a scripted video in the studio, then automate it in Make.com with Airtable topics, Perplexity research, a ChatGPT assistant script, HeyGen, a wait, a download, a YouTube upload with the AI label and a thumbnail. The automation fails twice because HeyGen's API rejects videos over 180 seconds on the presenter's plan, so the finished route is manual video creation. Links to HeyGen, ElevenLabs and Make.com include affiliate links, and the end pitches a coaching program.

17:23 Dec 24, 2025 304 views Save Hours Every Week With This YouTube Automation! Another n8n workflow that turns a YouTube video into a LinkedIn post, a newsletter and a detailed infographic: a form takes the URL, Apify fetches the transcript, Gemini summarizes it, KIE's Nano Banana Pro makes a 2K 16:9 infographic that is polled until ready and saved to Google Drive, and Claude Sonnet 4 writes the post and newsletter into a Google Doc. The presenter says it produced nearly 200,000 LinkedIn impressions in a month. That figure is self-reported, and posting stays manual.

9:23 Nov 12, 2025 849 views I Built a Fully Automated YouTube Shorts Machine in N8N! An n8n workflow that watches a Google Drive folder for new short clips, uploads each one to YouTube as unlisted, then generates a description, tags and title from the transcript and publishes it. The upload works, but the Apify transcript step fails in the demo, so the AI steps run without a transcript.

7:52 Nov 5, 2025 135 views Automate Your Entire Video Content Strategy With Sora 2 Add OpenAI's Sora 2 video generation to an n8n workflow. The presenter first updates a self-hosted n8n on a Hostinger VPS, because the Sora 2 option needs version 1.118.1, then builds a form that takes a prompt and product image and calls Sora 2 for an 8-second 1280 by 720 video. A bad request error turns out to be a negative OpenAI balance, fixed with a $6 top-up. The generated video does not match the product exactly.

12:50 Oct 17, 2025 588 views Sora 2 is Here: Create Professional AI Videos in Minutes A look at ways to try OpenAI's Sora 2 in October 2025. The presenter checks the official iOS app, Higgsfield, Sora2.run, Artlist and HeyGen and finds each needs a paid plan. No finished video is shown, and the one HeyGen attempt is blocked by Sora's content policy. The HeyGen link is an affiliate link, so the title's promise of professional videos in minutes is not delivered.

12:21 Sep 8, 2025 185 views The SEO Strategy You Need for More YouTube Views Improve the title and description of a YouTube video with a popular ChatGPT custom GPT for YouTube SEO, then recreate the same format with the OpenAI API when free usage runs out. The presenter edits the description, tests a title with a vidIQ score, tries Nano Banana on the thumbnail and advises changing one thing at a time. No view results are shown. The links in the description include affiliate links.

11:00 Aug 22, 2025 164 views This Make.com Hack Saved Me Hours on YouTube Descriptions A Make.com scenario that updates YouTube video descriptions automatically: it reads records with status to-do from Airtable, fetches each transcript with Dumpling AI, asks a custom OpenAI assistant to write an SEO description from a template, updates the video through the YouTube module and marks the Airtable record done. An OpenAI credit error is fixed with a $6 top-up. The scenario runs every five minutes and titles are not changed. The template costs $15.

18:42 Aug 12, 2025 1,624 views How to Use Syllaby to Build a Faceless Video Empire Walk through Syllaby video creation, script assistance, editing and scheduling, including its dashboard and content calendar.

31:46 Jul 21, 2025 371 views This AI System Generates YouTube Shorts on Complete Autopilot! A long Make.com build of a YouTube Shorts pipeline: Apify scrapes the latest videos of three AI-automation creators, Airtable stores them, an OpenAI assistant turns the most viewed titles into video ideas, GPT-4.1 writes scene-by-scene scripts, JSON2Video renders a vertical video and the file uploads to YouTube with an AI-generated label. The final run fails because the free JSON2Video quota is used up, so the presenter hardcodes an older render to show the download. The template costs $15, and HeyGen is suggested as an avatar alternative.

41:21 Jul 14, 2025 21,695 views Create Lifelike AI Avatars in Minutes (HeyGen Guide) Create an avatar video with HeyGen, then follow the Make.com workflow and its actual failures: a stale avatar ID and an API duration limit.

18:30 Jul 10, 2025 74 views YouTube Monetization Update: AI Content Is Getting Banned? A news-reading video from July 2025 on YouTube's announced update to Partner Program rules on inauthentic, mass-produced and repetitive content, taking effect July 15. The presenter reads several articles aloud (TechCrunch and others), adds opinions on AI avatar and faceless channels, and lists strategies the articles suggest: add human input, edit with care, transform reused material and disclose AI use. Exact policy wording had not been released at recording, and enforcement details are the articles' speculation. Nothing here is legal or policy advice.

14:38 Jul 3, 2025 2,653 views How to Scale Content with HeyGen + Make.com Automation Connect HeyGen and Make.com so an OpenAI assistant writes a script, HeyGen renders it with a custom avatar and voice clone, and a second scenario uploads it to YouTube as unlisted. Videos came out at 720p, and a resolution error was bypassed by hardcoding the video ID.

5:08 Jun 20, 2025 363 views Build Your Own YouTube Transcript Automation Today A Make.com scenario that reads YouTube links from Google Sheets, extracts transcripts with Dumpling AI, saves them to Google Drive and uploads them to an OpenAI vector store as a knowledge base. The goal is an ElevenLabs voice clone that answers WhatsApp messages, but the voice clone and WhatsApp parts are not built in this video. The template is offered in the presenter's free community.

15:16 Jun 13, 2025 68 views Generate Unlimited AI Videos With This Make.com Automation A Make.com scenario that makes faceless AI videos from Airtable topics and posts them: Airtable rows with status to-do, an OpenAI script, JSON2Video's toolbox to render a 720 by 1280 video, a wait for the render, an Airtable update with the video URL, and a router posting to a Facebook page and a YouTube channel. A test video on expat-friendly cities renders in about 60 to 70 seconds. The resolution is lowered to fit Make.com's 5 MB free plan file cap.

12:55 Jun 13, 2025 60 views I Built an AI That Finds Viral YouTube Topics (Here's What It Found) A Make.com scenario that finds video ideas from other creators' popular videos: it scrapes chosen YouTube channels with an Apify actor, stores titles and view counts in Airtable, asks an OpenAI assistant for ten similar ideas in JSON and saves them to a second Airtable table. The run produces idea lists for a travel and Thailand niche. A faceless video step is unlinked, the template is pay what you want, and the Make.com link is an affiliate link.

pages.excerpt: New AI model launches, tested 30 videos, newest first. Launch breakdowns and first tests of new models from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, xAI and others. When a new model ships, these videos cover what changed, what it costs, and how it handles a real build compared with the model it replaces. They include Claude, GPT, Gemini, Grok and open-weight releases such as Qwen, DeepSeek and GLM. Launch details change quickly, so check the provider’s own pricing and limits before you switch a production workload to a model you saw here. The written guides compare Claude models and show how to choose a model with a small test set. All videos Claude Code Codex and OpenCode n8n Make.com AI agents AI SEO Ea

8:16 Oct 13, 2026 716 views I Tested Meta Muse Wonder - Here's What Happened What Meta’s Muse Wonder model is, how its active memory, focus and coding features work, how it compares on Meta’s published benchmarks, and whether it is a real step forward for AI agents.

7:05 Oct 8, 2026 226 views Claude Haiku 5.5: Everything You Need To Know A walkthrough of Anthropic's Claude Haiku 5.5 announcement covering its benchmarks against Haiku 4.5, GPT-6 Luna and Sonnet 5.5, its pricing and where it is available. The model is not tested hands-on in this video.

9:53 Sep 30, 2026 348 views OpenAI Just Released Dots! Here's What You Need To Know A recap of OpenAI's September 29, 2026 dev day announcements and a first try of Dots, an always-on agent inside ChatGPT with its own cloud computer. The presenter customizes a dot, gets task suggestions drawn from past chats and email, and prepares a podcast application, though a site is blocked in the cloud browser. Prices, benchmarks and model claims are from OpenAI's recap. The presenter plans more videos before judging it.

7:50 Sep 29, 2026 245 views Claude Sonnet 5.5 Is Now Faster & Cheaper! A walkthrough of Anthropic's Claude Sonnet 5.5, announced as over 30 percent faster than Sonnet 5 and up to 30 percent cheaper for most work at the same $2 and $10 per million token price. The presenter reads Anthropic's benchmark charts, runs a side-by-side HTML game speed test against Sonnet 5, and recommends high effort for coding. The benchmark claims come from Anthropic's announcement.

8:24 Sep 24, 2026 253 views Claude Opus 5.5 Is Better And 40% Cheaper! A look at Claude Opus 5.5 two days after its announcement, using Anthropic's benchmark charts and pricing, then a live design audit of the presenter's homepage in the Claude desktop app with $100 of free cloud session credits. The quoted benchmarks come from Anthropic. The audit finds layout and copy bugs, and the fix plan is approved, but the results are not shown.

11:42 Sep 23, 2026 581 views GPT-6 Sol Is Here And It's 50% Cheaper! A walkthrough of OpenAI's announcement of GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna on September 23, 2026. Sol is priced at $2 per million input tokens, half its predecessor, and Luna at 10 cents. The presenter reads OpenAI's own benchmark charts against Opus 5 and Fable 5.1 and says Sol used 2 percent of a weekly limit. Benchmark and price figures are from the announcement and were not tested here.

10:57 Sep 22, 2026 412 views Grok 4.7 Is Officially Here And It's Powerful! A walkthrough of xAI's Grok 4.7 launch on September 22, 2026: benchmarks and prices from the announcement, demos by other users, and the presenter's attempt to use it through OpenRouter in Hermes Agent. The announced price is $2 per million input tokens and $6 for output. The presenter cannot see 4.7 in the Grok command line tool, only 4.6, and does not test coding quality.

6:44 Sep 12, 2026 587 views I Built A Rocket Launch Simulator Using GPT-6 Astra Build a single-file Three.js rocket launch simulator in GPT-6 Astra on medium mode from one 10,000-character prompt taken from Bridgebench. The first build takes about 23 minutes and runs with audio and quality settings. A follow-up prompt adds mouse zoom and rotation. The presenter says it looks decent but not very realistic, and wants clouds.

9:44 Sep 9, 2026 435 views ChatGPT Images 2.5 Is Faster Than Ever! A first test of ChatGPT Images 2.5, announced September 8, 2026, which OpenAI says is up to 50 percent faster than Images 2.0 and adds a Sketch feature. The presenter turns a rough drawing into a scene in about 25 seconds, makes an 80s photo, a caricature and a 3D toy avatar from a personal photo, and iterates on a YouTube thumbnail. Fetching a thumbnail by URL fails, and the final image is a little blurry.
12:48 Sep 6, 2026 4,977 views These 20 GPT-6 Astra Demos Are INSANE! Watch a selection of GPT-6 Astra demos, including interactive 3D models, generated interfaces and browser-based games.

9:52 Sep 4, 2026 364 views GPT-6 Astra Is Finally Here And It's Insane! A walkthrough of OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra launch, using the announcement page, OpenAI's demos and third-party benchmark charts. The presenter has not used the model yet because it has not rolled out to Codex or ChatGPT. Claims such as 99.9 percent on ARC-AGI-3 and the intelligence and cost rankings come from OpenAI and the charts shown.

4:43 Sep 3, 2026 216 views Claude Fable 5.1 Is Officially Here! A news summary of Claude Fable 5.1, released on September 2, 2026, read from Anthropic's press release and benchmark pages. Anthropic says it costs about 25 percent less than Fable 5, with larger savings on agentic work, and it needs usage credits rather than Pro or Max plans. The presenter's chart shows only a small intelligence lead over Opus 5, and they will mostly keep using cheaper models.

8:09 Sep 1, 2026 403 views I Tested The New DeepSeek Coding Harness (Is It Worth It?) A first run of DeepSeek's new agentic coding harness, in developer preview, where models, tools and skills are all plugins. It installs with npx and pnpm and opens a web UI on localhost. The DeepSeek balance is empty, the OpenCode key errors, and an OpenRouter key works with DeepSeek V4 Pro. The generated engine simulation is buggy and a fix is requested.
8:14 Jul 25, 2026 169 views Claude Opus 5 Is My New Go To Model! A rundown of Claude Opus 5: pricing against Fable 5, coding and reasoning benchmarks, visual reasoning, and real bug-fixing examples.

11:50 Jul 20, 2026 404 views I Tested Kimi K3 So You Don't Have To A look at Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 on release, mostly through benchmark pages and OpenCode Go. The presenter notes it is cheaper per token than Fable 5 but, in another creator's test, used about 21 million tokens against 3.5 million and ran three to four times longer. A site audit hits a priority queue limit, and signing in to the Kimi Code CLI fails.

8:10 Jul 16, 2026 185 views Grok 4.5 Is Actually Quite Impressive A first try of Grok 4.5 and the Grok command line tool, using a documentation prompt to build a single-file solar system app with satellites and asteroids from real-time data. Prices of $2 and $6 per million tokens and benchmark rankings are from xAI's article. The app works with some visual glitches, and the free daily usage limit is reached before the presenter can finish.

7:24 Jul 11, 2026 205 views GPT 5.6 Is Here And It's Pretty Insane! A look at OpenAI's GPT 5.6 release of July 9, 2026 with its Sol, Terra and Luna models, ChatGPT Work and the GPT Live voice model, from the news page and the Codex model picker. The presenter says they built a Chrome extension for their analytics app with GPT 5.6 in about an hour and a half and found credits last longer than with Fable 5. Benchmark and price figures come from OpenAI's materials.

10:24 Jul 4, 2026 1,574 views GLM 5.2 Now Has An Official Desktop App! Install ZCode, the official desktop app from Z.ai, and run GLM 5.2 on an existing project with plugins, skills, a built-in terminal and browser, and usage tracking. The test stays on the free plan, which the recording says includes 5 million GLM tokens per day.

14:57 Jul 3, 2026 319 views Claude Fable 5: Build Games in Seconds (Full Guide) Tips for getting more from Claude Fable 5 on limited credits after its July 2026 return: lower the effort level, use plan mode with the superpowers skill, give clear briefs, set goals and loops, and add the Compound Engineering plugin to Claude Code and Codex. The presenter also installs a CLAUDE.md improver, a memory optimizer and the Caveman skill, and falls back to Opus 4.8 for routine work. Claims about savings and about Fable being nerfed are not measured.

11:06 Jul 2, 2026 390 views Best Use Cases For Claude Fable 5 A hands-on session with Claude Fable 5 after its return, used in Claude Code at high effort for a security review and for a trial conversion and checkout review of the presenter's own web app. Sonnet writes the prompts, Fable 5 reports no critical, high or medium security findings in pending changes, then plans fixes for payment bugs. Fable 5 uses credits very quickly, reaching 95 to 98 percent of a session limit.

7:03 Jul 1, 2026 341 views Claude Fable 5 Is Back: What Changed? A news summary of Anthropic's announcement that Claude Fable 5 would return globally on the next day, read from the company's post and press coverage. It says Fable 5 comes back with new classifiers, some routine coding tasks fall back to Opus 4.8, and Pro, Max, Team and some Enterprise plans include it for up to 50 percent of weekly limits through July 7. The model had not returned when this was recorded.

8:44 Jun 30, 2026 6,318 views GLM 5.2 Inside OpenCode Go In Minutes! Select GLM 5.2 inside OpenCode on the Go plan, then use the same model in the OpenCode desktop app and in Hermes Agent. The free Zen option returned an insufficient balance error, so the test needed the Go plan, which costs $10 per month as stated in the recording.

9:09 Jun 29, 2026 321 views ChatGPT 5.6 Is Available, But Not For You! A news explainer on OpenAI's GPT 5.6, which is reported to be limited to about 20 pre-approved organizations through the API and Codex, with no paid ChatGPT tier unlocking it. The presenter attributes the staggered rollout to a US government request, based on reports and OpenAI's statements. Benchmark numbers and rollout rumors are repeated, not tested. The presenter advises staying with existing models and distrusting early access offers.

10:58 Jun 21, 2026 507 views Is GLM 5.2 The Best Opensource Model Ever? An overview of Z.AI's GLM 5.2 model and where to use it, mostly through OpenCode Go. The presenter reads benchmark pages and side-by-side demos made by another creator against Opus 4.8, and notes lower costs. The presenter had hit the OpenCode Go usage limit and does not run GLM 5.2 live, so the comparison rests on other people's results.

8:36 Jun 16, 2026 1,169 views Kimi K2.7 Code Vs DeepSeek V4 Pro: Is It Actually Better? Test Moonshot AI's Kimi K2.7 Code inside OpenCode by running a full site audit and then applying the fixes, while tracking cost against DeepSeek V4 Pro. It used credits much faster and hit the OpenCode Go monthly limit before the fixes were finished.

6:20 Jun 14, 2026 166 views Claude Fable 5 Banned By US Government! A news reaction to Anthropic's report that a US export control directive forced it to suspend access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for all foreign nationals, inside or outside the US. The presenter reads Anthropic's statement, which complies but disagrees, and adds speculation about causes that is not supported in the video. The title says banned, but the report describes a suspension for foreign nationals. A later video covers its return.

6:49 Jun 10, 2026 323 views Anthropic Just Released Claude Mythos (Is It Worth The Hype?) A news summary of Anthropic's June 9, 2026 launch of Claude Fable 5, which Anthropic calls a Mythos-class model with safeguards for general use. The presenter reads the press release and benchmark pages: it is included on paid plans until June 22, then needs usage credits, and costs $10 per million input tokens and $50 for output. The presenter had not used it yet. The title mentions Mythos, but the video is about Fable 5.

9:38 Apr 23, 2026 168 views CHATGPT IMAGES 2.0 Is Insanely Useful! A hands-on tour of ChatGPT Images 2.0 right after launch: OpenAI's sample prompts, the selection tool for editing part of an image, a caricature from a selfie, an aspect ratio change, a house blueprint from a photo, a sketch turned photorealistic and a book back cover whose generated ISBN barcode scans to the right listing. The leaderboard lead over Nano Banana Pro 2 is a claim from the video, and results vary between runs.

12:53 Nov 28, 2025 326 views I Challenged Gemini 3 To Build Classic Games | The Results Were Insane! Use Gemini 3 Pro Preview in Google AI Studio to build single-file HTML versions of Tetris, Snake, Asteroids and Pac-Man from prompts written in ChatGPT. Tetris, Snake and Asteroids each take a couple of minutes and play, though the snake looks like a Tetris block and Asteroids runs slowly. The Pac-Man version does not work. The presenter may host the games online.

6:24 Nov 27, 2025 105 views Gemini 3 Outperforming ChatGPT? Here's What I Found! A first look at Google's Gemini 3 in Google AI Studio, shortly after its November 18, 2025 release. The presenter reads the benchmark charts, has it redesign their landing page, builds a merch mockup app from a client's logo and deploys it to Google Cloud, and browses a gallery game. The landing page misses some details, and the claim that these tools will replace software engineers is the presenter's opinion.
